If you're like me, you've probably spent too much time on Wikipedia, clicking from one article to another and falling down rabbit holes. Now there's finally an official app — well, a widget — for that.

Finally, a button that takes you to a random Wikipedia article with just one tap.

Today's Wikipedia iOS app update adds a fun and practical new feature: a "random article" widget you can place on your iPhone or iPad home screen.

The widget comes in two sizes (small and medium), and there's a cute little mascot to keep you company.

Tap the widget and it jumps straight into a completely random Wikipedia article, automatically putting you into random mode.

No need to leave the app and tap the widget again. Just hit the random button and it'll roll the dice to fetch you a new article, letting you keep falling deeper and deeper down this "random rabbit hole."

Enjoy it — but be careful not to get too carried away! Earlier this summer, the Wikipedia app already added a history trivia game.

You can find this new widget in today's Wikipedia iPhone and iPad app update.
